name: HDFC Bank
summary: HDFC Bank hires for branch banking, sales and relationship-manager roles as well as technology, operations, credit and analytics. Candidates commonly report an online aptitude test or a screening interview, then one or two interviews on banking awareness, communication and sales ability, with customers and targets central for front-line roles. The bank publishes five core values: Customer Focus, Operational Excellence, Product Leadership, People and Sustainability.
rounds: Application through the careers site, a campus drive or a recruitment programme for some roles
Online aptitude test for many entry-level and programme roles, often covering reasoning, numbers, English and banking awareness
Interview with the hiring manager or a panel on your background, banking awareness and communication
For sales and relationship roles, often a role play or questions on handling customers and targets
HR discussion on fit, location and joining
Document and background checks before joining
looks_for: Comfort with sales targets and building customer relationships
Basic banking awareness: accounts, loans, interest rates and the RBI's role
Accuracy, compliance and honesty when handling customers' money
Willingness to work in different branches or cities

questions.text: Tell me about a time you convinced someone to try something new: a product, an idea or a change.
covers: Who they were and why they were hesitant
How you listened first, then made the case in their terms
The result, and what you learned about persuading people

questions.text: Describe a time you handled an upset customer or member of the public.
covers: What upset them, in their words
How you stayed calm, and what you did to solve the problem
How it ended and whether they came back

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were at risk of missing a target or deadline. What did you do?
covers: The target and when you saw you were behind
What you changed: effort, approach or asking for help
The outcome, and how you plan differently now

questions.text: Tell me about a time you caught an error in a document or calculation before it caused a problem.
covers: How you noticed it
How you checked it and who you told
What could have gone wrong, and the habit you keep because of it

questions.text: A customer has a large balance in a savings account and no plan for it. How would you approach the conversation?
covers: Asking about goals, time horizon, risk appetite and existing products
Options that suit them, such as fixed or recurring deposits, mutual funds or insurance, with risks explained
Not pushing an unsuitable product, and agreeing a follow-up

questions.text: What is the repo rate, and how does a change in it affect a bank's loans and deposits?
covers: The rate at which the RBI lends to banks
How changes pass through to loan rates and EMIs, especially loans linked to an external benchmark
Effects on deposit rates, demand for loans and the bank's margin

questions.text: What is KYC, and why must a bank complete it before opening an account?
covers: Verifying identity and address with valid documents, under RBI rules
Preventing fraud, money laundering and accounts in false names
Periodic updates and stricter checks for higher-risk customers

questions.text: How would you offer a credit card to a customer who says they don't want any debt?
covers: Listening and respecting the concern
Explaining responsible use, such as paying the full bill on time to avoid interest
Accepting a no gracefully, and noting their preference

questions.text: What is a non-performing asset, and why do banks watch them closely?
covers: A loan where interest or principal has been overdue beyond the RBI's limit, usually 90 days
Why it hurts: provisions reduce profit and tie up capital
How banks manage it: careful lending, early warning signs and collections

questions.text: How many home-loan customers could one branch in a mid-sized city like Nagpur serve in a year? Talk me through an estimate.
covers: Households in the branch's area and the share buying a home in a year
The share needing a loan and the branch's likely share of them
A check against how many applications staff can actually process

questions.text: For a technology role: how would you keep a mobile banking app working during a festive-season traffic spike?
covers: Forecasting load and load-testing before the season
Scaling the app layer, caching and queues to protect the core banking system
Monitoring, limiting less important features under strain, and telling customers if there's a problem

questions.text: Explain how a UPI payment moves from one bank account to another.
covers: The payer's app, the NPCI switch, the payer's bank and the payee's bank
The UPI ID and PIN, and the debit and credit steps
What happens when a payment is pending or fails, and how reversals work

questions.text: Introduce yourself and tell me why you'd suit a customer-facing role in a bank.
covers: Education and any work or internship in a few sentences
One example of working well with people
Why banking, and this role, is the next step

questions.text: Why HDFC Bank, and why banking as a career?
covers: Something specific about the bank: its products, reach or a value
What draws you to banking, shown by something you've done
Where you'd like to grow within the bank

questions.text: Are you comfortable working to a sales target and being posted to any branch or city?
covers: An honest answer, with any real constraint stated clearly
Evidence that you can handle targets, from study, work or a project
How you'd settle into a new place quickly

tips: Learn the five core values and have one example ready for Customer Focus and one for Operational Excellence.
Revise banking basics: repo rate, CRR, KYC, NPAs, types of deposits and loans, and UPI.
For sales roles, be honest about targets: explain how you'd build a customer base rather than promising you'd never miss one.
Read the bank's recent press releases and RBI announcements so you can talk about current banking news.
Apply only through official channels; a request to pay money for an interview or offer letter is a warning sign of fraud.
Prepare a short, calm explanation for any gap year or change of stream.
